entries.remark: Work done per unit test charge in bringing it from infinity to a point.

entries.quantity: Potential due to a Point Charge
entries.remark: Potential at a distance r from a point charge Q. Potential is zero at infinity.

entries.quantity: Potential due to an Electric Dipole
entries.remark: Potential depends on the angle θ between the position vector r and dipole moment p.
Electric field is in the direction where potential decreases steepest. Its magnitude is the change in potential per unit displacement.
Work stored in assembling two charges q₁ and q₂ at a distance r₁₂ apart.
Ratio of charge Q on a conductor to the potential difference V. Unit is Farad (F).
A is the area of plates and d is the separation between them (for vacuum).
Capacitance increases by a factor of K (dielectric constant) when the medium is filled with a dielectric.
The reciprocal of equivalent capacitance is the sum of the reciprocals of individual capacitances.
The total capacitance is the sum of the individual capacitances.
Energy stored in the electric field between the plates of a charged capacitor.

entries.dimension: The first law states the incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane. The second law states the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
Occurs on highly smooth surfaces like mirrors. Light rays remain parallel after reflection, creating a clear and sharp image.
Occurs on rough surfaces. While each individual ray follows the law of reflection, the surface irregularities scatter light in many directions.
